tags.gist: Supports exploring competency assessment if anchored in real workflows, intended use, human rights and clear accountability so clinicians do not bear sole liability.
Says effective premarket oversight needs a valid clinical association established before any analytical benchmarking.
Says postmarket monitoring must verify premarket performance, never substitute for deficient premarket evidence.
Restates support for exploring competency assessment, conditioned on anchoring in workflows, intended use, human rights and accountability lines protecting clinicians and hospitals.
Restates that a valid clinical association must be established before analytical benchmarking.
Restates that monitoring verifies premarket performance rather than replacing missing premarket evidence.
Applauds recent oversight updates, pilots and sandboxes, but wants any flexibility strictly contingent on robust premarket clinical evidence and independent verification.
Recommends risk assessment be based on the device's intended use, clinical task and real-world workflow.
Recommends establishing clinical association before any benchmarking or setting of premarket evidence levels.
Recommends evaluating human-AI interactions and agentic workflows holistically, including multi-turn conversational trajectories.
Recommends requiring risk-proportionate clinical validation, from retrospective review to prospective study, for all devices before market entry.
Recommends mandatory transparency and disclosure from foundation model developers on training data, safety limits and updates.
Recommends independent third parties verify benchmarking, fairness and performance of medium- and high-risk devices, mitigating conflicts of interest.
Recommends designing monitoring to verify premarket claims and detect drift, not to stand in for inadequate premarket evidence.
Answers no: wants intended use and scope added as explicit considerations, plus reversibility, human intervention, time pressure and traceability.
Would judge directiveness by real-world workflow, measuring how often clinicians override outputs, with disclaimers never counted as mitigation.
Would treat patient-facing tools on high-stakes topics as higher risk, anchored in task and error impact rather than user role, with mandated safeguards.
Prefers a focus on intended use and on the qualifications needed for safe use over a generalist-versus-specialist distinction, with institutional controls.
Wants whole conversations evaluated by multi-turn simulation for drift and escalation, with intended use stating conversation limits such as turns and advice types.
Wants missed and unnecessary escalations measured separately in benchmarks, balanced by clinical context.
Wants intended use and clinical association established through a research study, as under existing device regulations, before benchmarking and risk classification.
Conditions support on proportionality, institutional readiness with regulatory expertise and quality systems before deployment, and benchmarking always paired with clinical confirmation.
Says the two-axis framework cannot stand alone and is meaningful only after clinical association; all devices need both validations, with confirmation rigor scaling.
Calls Q9 the wrong problem: the issue is whether benchmarks predict deployment; wants prospective clinical-association analyses and acceptance criteria before benchmarking.
Asks FDA to bring back the archived Clinical Evaluation guidance for software as a medical device.
Wants benchmark cases compared with real cases, real-world performance tracked against predictions, independent experts reviewing sponsor benchmarks, and synthetic data documented.
Wants clinical confirmation required for all devices, lighter for low risk, prospective for high risk, always covering the intended populations.
Says clinical association must precede any sample-size question; then verify representativeness, define acceptable performance and collect until confidence is met.
Allows synthetic data for variations and stress tests, not subgroup or safety validation; wants real-data fairness assessment as an approval condition for high-risk devices.
Prefers ground truth where it exists, median clinician otherwise, specialists for high stakes, and structured expert opinion for novel areas, all prespecified.
Accepts status quo, delayed specialist review or no-intervention comparators under IRB oversight when prespecified and justified for the intended use.
Would require independent third parties, not AI tools, for benchmarking verification, clinician validation and fairness review of medium- and high-risk devices.
Says the framework adapts to multimodal and predictive systems, adding cross-modal consistency checks, bounded variability and confirmation of predicted trajectories.
Sets premarket evidence by tier: benchmarking alone for low risk, plus one confirmation method for medium, plus a prospective study for high risk.
Strongly recommends against monitoring as a stand-in for inadequate premarket evidence, and against conditional approval pending postmarket data.
Sets cadences by risk: annual review for low risk, quarterly re-benchmarking for medium, monthly drift tracking and semi-annual fairness audits for high.
Lets machine agents collect metrics, flag threshold breaches and report, but not judge importance or decide changes; GenAI monitors need independent testing.
Wants explicit roles so clinicians and hospitals do not absorb sole liability: manufacturers monitor and act, institutions train and limit access, FDA enforces.
Would give small prompt or data updates focused retesting within PCCPs, while new uses, populations or major model changes need submission and IRB review.
Proposes a tiered PCCP keyed to accuracy change bands including subgroups, from no submission to expedited to full review, with continuous monitoring against thresholds.
Keeps the manufacturer responsible, with contracts requiring notice, rollback access, safety disclosures, audit rights and performance guarantees from developers.
Says voluntary master files will not work; wants mandatory disclosure of model identity, training data categories, limitations and contractual commitments before approval.
Wants required testing of multi-step behavior, tool use, approval points and stop ability, with audit trails, clinician review and escalation before irreversible actions.
Concludes the framework should prioritize clinical association, workflow-based validation and strict accountability for models over mere benchmarking.
